description: Issue #839: with THREE declarations of `step`, the run halts at the SECOND (line 4) — the first collision in source order — and `params.original_span` names line 1. A rule that reported the LAST declaration, or that scanned the whole program and flagged every copy, would not stop here. What this fixture deliberately does NOT claim: that `original_span` is the FIRST declaration rather than the most recent one seen. At run time those two are indistinguishable, because execution halts at the first duplicate and so the map only ever holds first declarations — a mutation making the runtime record "most recent" passes this fixture and the whole corpus, which is how that was established rather than assumed. The first-vs-most-recent property is observable only where every finding is reported, and it is pinned at check stage by `core-language/check/duplicate-definition-not-profile-gated` and `data/check/duplicate-definition-across-declaration-slots`, each of which declares one name three times so that BOTH later findings name the first declaration rather than the one before them. The three bodies print different values so the fixture also stays sensitive to any override rule sneaking back in.

diagnostics.message: you already defined step on line 1.
